I'd like to discuss our plans for MPLEX deprecation and (possibly) TCP transport deprecation (based on conversation happening [here](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3866)).

Currently, in Teku, we have full support for QUIC but not for Yamux (only an experimental implementation). So our only option when a peer does not support QUIC is to fall back to TCP/MPLEX.

The direction so far seems to be to completely eliminate TCP transport. From a technical standpoint, Teku is ok with that now that we have full support for QUIC (it is de facto our default transport now). However, we do notice that not all users have their network configuration set up to enable UDP, and some have restrictions that might prevent them from doing so without proper changes to their infrastructure. So my gut feeling is that, for us to safely eliminate TCP from our CL stack, we would need a more elaborate rollout plan, possibly with additional metrics and clearer communication around this change. So, anything for Glamsterdam seems to be too close already?

What I suggested in the ticket I mentioned before, assuming we do want to eliminate TCP from our stack, is to:
1. Announce TCP/MPLEX/Yamux deprecation;
2. All CLs using QUIC as their default dial path for Glamsterdam;
3. Each client will have until Hegota to finish deprecation (either with intermediary releases if they feel confident or at Hegota).

I won't be at the call, but I'll try to have someone from Teku up-to-date on the matter to participate in the discussion. Otherwise, we should at least get all client teams attention to https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3866.

I would like to ask ACD permission to PFI [EIP-8411](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12299) Fast payload broadcast

More context: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2211#issuecomment-5601739597

Lighthouse team ranking of the CL EIPs proposed for Hegotá: [https://hackmd.io/@kingy/SkXFUWOFzg](https://hackmd.io/@kingy/SkXFUWOFzg) Forkcast **: ** EIP-8411 does not yet appear in the Forkcast tool, and we rank it A. EIP-8383 and EIP-8369 we rank B and D respectively
Nimbus rankings: https://forkcast.org/rank/#r=S:8015,8379;A:8365,8371;B:7716;C:8025,8148,8205;D:8142,8146,8237,8243,8333,8334,8363,8375 Edit: we've been asked about quick slots. DFI:

There is a [thread](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1549712825180758018/1549713776591241287) on discord suggesting to reduce the scope of EIP-8365 (BLS withdrawal credential retirement) to the 0x00 deposit guard only, and drop the exit of existing 0x00 validators to a later fork. Since client teams have already assessed the EIP at its current scope in their rankings, I want to gauge interest before making a change this large.

I believe other members of lodestar, [prysm](https://hackmd.io/@ttsao/prysm-view-hegota#EIP-8365-BLS-Withdrawal-Credential-Retirement-conditional) and [lighthouse](https://hackmd.io/@kingy/SkXFUWOFzg#A-tier) prefer the reduction of the EIP scope.
